resolved_by: The Sentencing Commission resolved the split by promulgating Amendment 794 (effective Nov. 1, 2015), which revised the § 3B1.2 commentary to compare the defendant only with other participants in the same criminal activity.
issue: When deciding whether a defendant qualifies for a mitigating-role reduction under U.S.S.G. § 3B1.2, is the 'average participant' limited to those who took part in the same criminal activity, or does it also include the universe of persons who commit similar crimes?

sides.position: The 'average participant' means only those who actually participated in the criminal activity at issue, so the defendant's culpability is measured only against co-participants in the case (the approach the Commission adopted in Amendment 794).
cases: United States v. Nkome, 987 F.3d 1262 (10th Cir. 2021)

sides.position: The 'average participant' also includes the universe of persons participating in similar crimes, so the defendant's culpability is considered relative both to co-participants and to the typical offender.
cases: United States v. Santos, 357 F.3d 136 (1st Cir. 2004)

quote: But others “concluded that the ‘average participant’ also includes the ‘universe of persons participating in similar crimes.’” Id.
cite: United States v. Nkome, 987 F.3d 1262 (10th Cir. 2021)
